title: CAN bus and ESP32 TWAI: automotive and industrial networks

questions.prompt: Which option states the main idea of “CAN bus and ESP32 TWAI: automotive and industrial networks” correctly?
options: UART is asynchronous point-to-point serial using TX/RX and common ground
1-Wire connects compatible devices on one bus with few wires.
I2S carries digital audio using bit clock (BCLK), word select (WS/LRCLK), and data lines.
CAN is a noise-tolerant differential, message-based bus used in vehicle ECUs, industrial control, and robotics.
questions.answer: CAN is a noise-tolerant differential, message-based bus used in vehicle ECUs, industrial control, and robotics.
questions.explanation: CAN is a noise-tolerant differential, message-based bus used in vehicle ECUs, industrial control, and robotics.

questions.prompt: Which additional fact about “CAN bus and ESP32 TWAI: automotive and industrial networks” is accurate?
options: It connects digital microphones, DACs, and audio codecs
ESP32 calls its CAN 2.0 controller peripheral TWAI
DS18B20 measures temperature digitally and has a unique identifier.
questions.answer: ESP32 calls its CAN 2.0 controller peripheral TWAI
questions.explanation: ESP32 calls its CAN 2.0 controller peripheral TWAI

questions.prompt: Which practical detail should be considered when using “CAN bus and ESP32 TWAI: automotive and industrial networks”?
options: it is not UART or I2C.
The data line needs a suitable pull-up
controller pins cannot connect directly to CAN wiring.
I2C shares SDA/SCL and addresses among devices and needs pull-ups.
questions.answer: controller pins cannot connect directly to CAN wiring.
questions.explanation: controller pins cannot connect directly to CAN wiring.
